name: Barghest
body: A monstrous black dog said to haunt lonely roads and churchyards across northern England. To see it once is an ill sign; to see it twice is said to mark the seer for death before the year is out.

name: Wendigo
body: An Algonquian spirit of the deep winter woods, born from starvation and the taboo of eating human flesh. The more it consumes, the hungrier and larger it grows, forever starving no matter how much it takes.

name: Tengu
body: A bird-like yokai of the high mountain forests, equal parts protector and prankster. Older tengu are said to have taught swordsmanship to the heroes of old, testing their pride before their skill.

name: Peri
body: A winged being of Persian legend, too beautiful for cruelty and barred from paradise until it completes a penance. Peris are said to live on the scent of perfume alone, guiding travellers lost beneath the stars.

name: Chort
body: A horned devil of Slavic folk belief, more mischievous than truly evil, fond of striking foolish bargains with the greedy and the proud. Its name became a byword for reckless risk: to go 'to the chort' is to court disaster.

name: Rakshasa
body: A shape-changing demon of Indian epic, able to wear any face while its own remains monstrous underneath. The Ramayana names entire kingdoms of them, ruled by kings who could only be undone by cunning or divine weapons.

name: Haetae
body: A lion-like beast of Korean tradition believed to sense right from wrong on sight, said to bite the guilty and spare the innocent. Its statues still guard palace gates, watching for both injustice and fire.

name: Naga
body: A serpent people said to rule the rivers and the world beneath them, capable of taking human form to walk among mortals. Naga are honoured as much as feared, since an insulted river spirit can flood a season's harvest.

name: Selkie
body: A seal that sheds its skin to walk ashore as a woman or man, bound to the sea for as long as the skin is hidden. Island tales tell of fishermen who stole a selkie's skin for a wife, and of the grief that followed when she found it again.

name: Kappa
body: A small water-dwelling yokai with a dish of water atop its head that holds its strength. Spill the water and a kappa loses its power entirely, which is exactly the trick used to turn its own mischief against it.

name: Banshee
body: A wailing spirit attached to certain old Irish families, her cry heard the night before a death in the household. She grieves not out of malice but duty, mourning a loss that has not yet happened.

name: Manticore
body: A lion-bodied beast with a human face and a tail of venomous spines, first described by a Greek physician retelling Persian traveller's tales. It was said to devour its prey whole, leaving no trace behind.

name: Griffin
body: Eagle above and lion below, the griffin was said to nest in the mountains where gold was mined, fiercely guarding hoards from thieves. Its image became a mark of nobility across the ancient world, prized for its loyalty as much as its strength.

name: Basilisk
body: Called the king of serpents, small enough to overlook but lethal enough that its gaze alone could turn flesh to stone. Medieval bestiaries claimed only the crow of a rooster or the sight of its own reflection could kill it.

name: Chimera
body: Lion, goat and serpent fused into one fire-breathing terror, born of monstrous parents and slain by the hero Bellerophon from the back of Pegasus. Its very name became the word for any hopeless, ill-fitting combination.

name: Harpy
body: Winged women with the talons of birds of prey, sent by the gods to snatch food from the plates of the oath-breaker Phineus. Sailors blamed sudden squalls on their passing, never quite seen, always felt.

name: Cyclops
body: A one-eyed giant of immense strength, remembered both as the forge-hands who armed Zeus with thunderbolts and as the isolated shepherd Polyphemus, blinded by Odysseus's cunning rather than his sword.

name: Minotaur
body: Half man, half bull, born of a queen's curse and hidden at the centre of a labyrinth built to contain it. Every nine years it was given a tribute of youths, until Theseus followed a thread back out of the maze having ended it.

name: Gorgon
body: Three monstrous sisters with serpents for hair, of whom only Medusa was mortal. To meet her eyes was to turn to stone, until Perseus took her head using nothing but a mirrored shield to avoid her gaze directly.

name: Siren
body: Sea maidens whose song was so beautiful that sailors steered their ships onto the rocks to reach it. Odysseus survived them only by having his crew bind him to the mast while their ears were sealed with wax.

name: Leviathan
body: A sea monster of such scale in Hebrew scripture that its coils were said to encircle the deep itself, tamed only by the hand of God. Later tradition names it as one of the great beasts destined to be served at the final feast of the righteous.

name: Behemoth
body: Leviathan's counterpart on dry land, a beast of such strength that scripture describes its bones as bars of iron. It eats grass like an ox yet cannot be caught by any hook or snare devised by mortal hands.

name: Ifrit
body: A powerful class of jinn said to be made of smokeless fire, proud and often hostile to mortals who trespass on their domain. The tales of a Thousand and One Nights are full of ifrit bound by seals of Solomon into jars and lamps.

name: Djinn
body: A being of free will created from fire, living alongside humanity in a parallel world of deserts and ruins. Some are pious, some are wicked, and all are said to grant favours only at a price the asker rarely anticipates.

name: Nuckelavee
body: An Orcadian sea demon with no skin, its raw muscle and black blood visible as it rides a horse fused to its own body. Islanders blamed it for crop blight and horse plague, and it was said to fear only fresh water and burning kelp smoke.

name: Aswang
body: A shapeshifting ghoul of Filipino folklore that appears ordinary by day and hunts by night, often blamed for stillbirths and missing livestock. Garlic, salt, and the sting of a stingray tail were the traditional wards against it.

name: Tikbalang
body: A horse-headed creature of the deep forest, tall as the trees themselves, that delights in confusing travellers until they walk in circles. Turning one's shirt inside out is the old remedy said to break its spell.

name: Alux
body: A small Maya spirit invited to guard a new field or home, honoured with offerings for seven years before being sealed away with a tiny door. Left unappeased, it turns from helpful guardian to relentless prankster.

name: Chullachaqui
body: A guardian spirit of the Amazon rainforest that can take the shape of a friend or relative to lure travellers off their path. Hunters are taught to check for its telltale mismatched feet before following anyone too far into the trees.

name: Popobawa
body: A one-eyed, bat-winged shadow said to stalk the island of Zanzibar by night, its name meaning 'bat-wing' in Swahili. Waves of reported sightings have spread panic through entire villages within living memory.

name: Nagual
body: A person's animal spirit-double in Mesoamerican belief, bound so closely to its human counterpart that a wound to one appears on the other. Sorcerers were said to train the gift deliberately, walking as jaguars by night.

name: Kelpie
body: A shapeshifting water horse that lures riders onto its back before plunging into the loch, its skin turning to sticky tar the moment they are trapped. Some tales soften it into a guardian of the water, punishing only the reckless.

name: Redcap
body: A murderous goblin of the border ruins, said to dye its cap in the blood of travellers and lose its strength entirely if the dye ever dries out. It is driven off only by scripture, a crucifix, or the light of a new day.

name: Boggart
body: A house spirit that turns from helpful to spiteful the moment it is named or thanked, souring milk and hiding household tools out of pure spite. Families were advised never to speak its presence aloud, lest it grow bold.

name: Brownie
body: A shaggy household spirit that completes chores overnight in exchange for a bowl of cream left by the hearth. Offer it clothing as a gift, however, and it takes deep offence, vanishing from the house for good.

name: Dryad
body: A nymph bound to a single tree, born and dying alongside it, her wellbeing tied so closely to the wood that harming the tree harms her in turn. Woodcutters who respected certain ancient groves believed a dryad's favour brought good fortune.

name: Naiad
body: A nymph of springs, streams and fountains, her presence said to keep the water pure and sweet. To offend a naiad was to risk a spring running dry or turning brackish overnight.

name: Cait Sidhe
body: A great black fairy cat of Highland legend, believed to steal the soul of the newly dead if allowed to pass over the body before burial. Wakes were kept noisy and well-lit through the night specifically to keep it away.

name: Yeti
body: A great ape-like figure said to roam the high snows of the Himalaya, glimpsed only as footprints in fresh powder or a distant silhouette against the ridgeline. Sherpa tradition treats it less as a monster than as a rightful, private resident of the peaks.

name: Oni
body: A horned ogre of Japanese folklore, red or blue-skinned and armed with an iron club, said to punish wrongdoers in the underworld and haunt the unlucky northeast gate of a home. Bean-throwing rituals at the turn of the year still drive them off each winter.
